newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil steady to softer, Mediterranean firmer.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil steady to softer, Mediterranean firmer.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices were unchanged to slightly softer on Wednesday. Traders said tighter ARA supplies pegged barge and cargo premiums to a slightly softer benchmark gas oil futures but trade was thin.
On the key ARA market brokers said prompt barge supplies were becoming fairly tight although this was balanced for the time-being with a stronger dollar stifling demand from Germany.
Trade house short covering saw barges trade at a steady premium of $1.50 to the July IPE screen in early business but otherwise trade was thin with the market offered over at the level in late trade.
Diesel barges valued around July IPE +$5 a tonne fob ARA.

Diesel cargo prices held steady with values for prompt deliveries pegged around July IPE +$4 a tonne cif Rotterdam. 0.2 sulphur cargo differentials were steady around August IPE +$1/+2 a tonne cif NWE.
In the Mediterranean gas oil prices were firmer with supportive buying into Italy and Spain and recent demand for product to fill tenders into Turkey and a Greece leaving supplies generally tighter.
Traders said diesel's narrow differential to 0.2 sulphur oil was also adding to the tightness.
"Refiners are reluctant to run EN590 while the differential to 0.2 sulphur material is so small" one trader said
